_comment: Ratchet gates: CI fails only when the count of a known-bad pattern rises
above the committed baseline below. Policy and number change in one diff.
Run: node scripts/ratchet.mjs        (gate — used by CI and make ratchet)
node scripts/ratchet.mjs --list  (print every site, incl. allowed)
node scripts/ratchet.mjs --update  (lower baselines to match reality;
refuses to raise them)
A count BELOW baseline also fails ('slack') — otherwise a newly introduced
bad site could hide under headroom left by an unrelated fix. Run --update
to resync the baseline whenever the count legitimately changes.
Exempt a specific line with an inline comment: `ratchet-allow: <reason>`.
Allowed sites are still counted and listed separately with --list.
roots: git-tracked file roots ratchet.mjs scans (via `git ls-files -- <roots>`).
An empty template (no files under any root) scans 0 files: baseline 0 passes,
baseline > 0 fails as 'scan roots vanished — refusing to pass'.
kind: pattern     — whole-file-content regex per extension group.
kind: unreferenced — heuristic: a testGlobs match is 'orphaned' when neither
its full path nor any parent directory appears as a substring in any
wiring file (.github/workflows/*.yml, Makefile, package.json,
pyproject.toml, or any non-test file under the scanned roots — a
'runner script'). A bare directory reference wires everything beneath it.
This is a heuristic, not static analysis — auto-discovering test runners
(glob-based, like scripts/dev/board/tests/run-all.sh) make true orphans
rare, since pointing at the containing directory is enough to wire them.
When a project adopts a linter, prefer its native rule over the pattern
entry below (ruff S110 for Python, eslint no-empty for JS/TS) — see
'Enforcement' in .claude/rules/error-handling.md.

patterns.label: python: bare except swallowed with pass
